correctness.rationale: For integer alphabet q>=2 and n>=4, set g_n=log(M_n(q))/n. Möbius inversion yields M_n=(q^n/n)(1+r_n), with |r_n| bounded by a geometric series of proper-divisor terms. The exact second-difference inequality D_n=g_(n+2)-2g_(n+1)+g_n< -L(n)+E(n,q), L=(2log n-3)/(n+2)^3 and E=[2q/((q-1)n q^(n/2))]*(1+2q^(-1/2)+q^-1), proves all n>=6 for q>=9 and all n>=23 for q>=2 by two strict ratio inductions. Exact small signs D_3>0, D_4<0, D_5<0 for q>=6; independently recomputed all 115 missing strict sign tests q=2..8, n=T(q)..22 and seven reverse witnesses D_(T-1)>0 by integer powers. Thus T(2)=14,T(3)=8,T(4,5)=6,T(q>=6)=4 are genuine smallest infinite tails; q restricted to integer, finite certificate used only for finite remainder.
